clue.text: Ready to complain, losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for complain drops its first letter

parts.note: to gripe is to complain

explanation.surface: Someone is all set to start moaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe means fully prepared or ready, as in a plan ripe for action.

clue.text: Declining to accept a lot of commotion — genuine about that

indicators.note: about that means the word for genuine goes around the shortened commotion

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: a lot of, not all, so the word for commotion loses its last letter

parts.note: a fuss is a commotion

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to put up with a big fuss, sincerely meaning it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declining' is a noun sense here, the act of saying no, not a falling off.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is the act of declining to accept an offer or request.

clue.text: Shortage of staff restricting chores when working in nursery

indicators.note: restricting means the shortened staff confines the reworked chores within it
a shortage means the word for staff falls short by its last letter

parts.note: a pole is a staff or stick

indicators.note: working means the letters of chores are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A nursery is understaffed, so the chores pile up while it is open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursery' is used as an adjective, as in nursery education, rather than a room or a plant seller.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery is used adjectivally of education for children below school age, the same as preschool.

clue.text: Copper perhaps, crashing tractor into drink

indicators.note: into means the reworked tractor goes inside the word for drink

parts.note: tea is a drink

indicators.note: crashing means the letters of tractor are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A policeman, perhaps, drives a tractor into a pool of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is a reddish-brown colour; terracotta is an example of such a shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is a brownish-orange colour, so it is given as one example of a copper-like hue.

clue.text: Rascal in time will make mistakes

indicators.note: in means the rascal is placed inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a rascal or scoundrel

explanation.surface: A warning that a rogue will slip up given enough time.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed errors in a printed book, so the word is a plural for mistakes.

clue.text: Country memorial housing a tavern

indicators.note: housing means the memorial holds the tavern within it

parts.note: a relic is a memorial or keepsake of the past
a pub is a tavern

explanation.surface: A national monument that has a bar inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state or nation governed without a monarch.

clue.text: Get ready to shoot a picture, opening mostly depicting crow

parts.note: to cock a gun is to get it ready to fire
a doodle is an idle picture

indicators.note: mostly means the word for opening loses its last letter

parts.note: a door is an opening

explanation.surface: A photographer prepares to take a shot of a crow at a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crow' is a verb here, the rooster's call, not the bird; 'mostly' cuts DOOR to DOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of a rooster is its crow, rendered in English as this imitative phrase.

clue.text: Recording movement of yacht around river

indicators.note: around means the yacht's manoeuvre wraps about the river letter

parts.note: a tack is a change of course by a sailing boat
R is a map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A log of a yacht's manoeuvres as it rounds a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is a single recorded song on an album.

clue.text: Forward missing header collared by supporter with a keen eye

indicators.note: collared by means the shortened word sits inside the word for supporter, like a neck in a collar

parts.note: an ally is a supporter

indicators.note: missing its header means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: pert means forward or cheeky

explanation.surface: A football forward, caught out without heading the ball, is grabbed by a fan who spots everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' is not a footballer but the adjective meaning cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something alertly means doing it watchfully, with full attention.

clue.text: Dessert needing Chartreuse — lots — sloshed

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A pudding that needs plenty of liqueur, served by someone already tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Chartreuse is a French herbal liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte russe is a cold pudding of sponge fingers filled with custard or cream.

clue.text: Subsequent payment, though not in regard to student

indicators.note: though not means the letters for in regard to are left out

parts.note: a refresher is a further fee paid to a barrister in a long case
re means in regard to, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A later payment that has nothing to do with a student.
explanation.walkthrough: A refresher, in British legal usage, is an extra fee paid to counsel as a case runs on.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a fresher is a first-year university student.

clue.text: Press to join mature holiday scheme

parts.note: to pack is to press tightly together
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A journalist signs up for an over-fifties holiday deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A package is an all-inclusive holiday with travel and lodging sold together.

clue.text: Source of protection potentially rickety and unstable

indicators.note: potentially means these letters could form something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A defence that could prove shaky and unsafe.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's comfort blanket, and figuratively anything giving reassurance, provides a sense of protection.

clue.text: Observe — it's acceptable to block fool

indicators.note: to block means the word for acceptable is stuck in the middle of the fool

parts.note: a loon is a fool
OK means it is acceptable

explanation.surface: Watching someone decide whether it is fine to stop an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: To look on is to watch as a spectator, the same as observe.

clue.text: Youth, or one coming in fresh?

indicators.note: coming in means the two pieces enter the word for fresh

parts.note: minty means fresh in taste
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking whether youth means someone new arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Minority is the state of being under legal age, i.e. a person's youth.

clue.text: Exotic lover? Over being embraced by a Martian that's besotted

indicators.note: being embraced by means the letter for over goes inside the muddled alien
besotted, here as if drunk, means the letters of a Martian are muddled into a new order

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A lover from afar who has fallen for a smitten Martian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic' points to the word being Italian rather than to an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Inamorata is an Italian loanword for a woman who is someone's beloved, hence a foreign-sounding term.

clue.text: Give less attention to Northern Irish drama?

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: Asking whether a play from Northern Ireland deserves less notice.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To downplay something is to minimise it, making it seem less important.

clue.text: Recalled brief comment about hot TV show

indicators.note: about means the reversed comment goes around the letter for hot
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a notelet is a short note
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A retracted short remark about a sizzling television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns NOTELET into TELETON, and 'about' wraps that around H.
explanation.definitionFit: A telethon is a long television broadcast raising money for charity.

clue.text: Operations in stern or other part of vessel

indicators.note: in means the operations are placed inside the word for stern

parts.note: the tail is the rear or stern
ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: Work going on at the back of a ship or elsewhere aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest sail on a mast, so it is a part of a ship.

clue.text: Old King heading for European conflict in days

indicators.note: heading for means take the first letter of European
in means the letters go inside the abbreviation for days

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for day, doubled for days
war is a conflict

explanation.surface: A former monarch leading Europe into conflict for days on end.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is the name of several English kings of the past.

clue.text: Actually, excellent performer has run off

parts.note: def is slang for excellent

indicators.note: off means the letter for run is removed from the performer

parts.note: an actor is a performer
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A star player has, in truth, fled.
explanation.definitionFit: De facto is Latin for 'in fact', describing what is true in reality.

clue.text: Goes off climbing, keeping to a higher level in sort of fog?

indicators.note: keeping means the reversed word holds the other piece inside
climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: rots means goes off, as food does
up means to a higher level

explanation.surface: Something rots as it rises above a sort of mist.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' reads a word from bottom to top; the question mark flags that fog is figurative.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed state, figuratively a mental haze or fog.

clue.text: Story of boy's encounter with animal, domestic one — he went for lad, unfortunately

definitions.text: Story of boy's encounter with animal

parts.note: a pet is a domestic animal

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tale of a boy meeting a beast, one that sadly attacked the lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter and the Wolf is Prokofiev's musical tale of a boy who catches a wolf.

clue.text: Monotonous sound of personnel in corporation

indicators.note: in means the personnel letters sit inside the word for corporation

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a paunch, and tum is a belly
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: A dull drone from the staff at a large company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company but is jokey slang for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a steady, repetitive humming noise.

clue.text: Love, in different ways, being swamped in a lake's spray

indicators.note: being swamped in means the love letters are engulfed by the outer pieces

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
love is given two ways: Eros, god of love, and O, love as a zero tennis score

explanation.surface: A romance played out in various ways, drowned in the spray of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a can that releases its contents as a fine spray.

clue.text: Reduced charge securing very large article with little sparkle?

indicators.note: securing means the shortened charge holds the other pieces inside it
reduced means the word for charge loses its last letter

parts.note: a price is a charge
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A cut-price fee for a huge item that hardly glitters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' looks like a discount on the charge but signals a dropped final letter; OS (outsize) is a British clothing size label.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means dull and unimaginative, lacking any spark.

clue.text: Slowly move cart backwards, attaining timber store

parts.note: to lumber is to move heavily and slowly

indicators.note: backwards means the word for cart is read from end to start

parts.note: a dray is a heavy cart

explanation.surface: A cart is reversed slowly into a wood depot.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberyard is a place where cut wood is kept and sold.

clue.text: Dressing medic must stock indeed

indicators.note: must stock means the medic holds the other word inside

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
ay is an old word for yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A doctor really ought to keep bandages in supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' looks like a bandage but is salad dressing, short for mayonnaise.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is informal for mayonnaise, a creamy sauce used on salads.
